title: Necessity of the log n Factor in the Guth-Katz Distance Bound

problemStatement.formal: \text{For } n \text{ points in } \mathbb{R}^2 \text{ with distance multiplicities } f(u_i), \text{ Guth-Katz gives } \sum_i f(u_i)^2 \le C n^3 \log n. \text{ Is the } \log n \text{ necessary? The } \sqrt{n}\times\sqrt{n} \text{ lattice attains } \sum_i f(u_i)^2 \ge c\, n^3 \log n, \text{ so it cannot be removed in general.}
problemStatement.plain: The Guth-Katz theorem bounds the sum of squared distance-multiplicities of n planar points by about n^3 log n. We ask whether the extra log n factor is intrinsic. For the square integer grid it is: the grid actually achieves ~n^3 log n, so the log cannot be removed in general. The refined question is whether it disappears for configurations that avoid lattice-like additive structure.
whyMatters: Pins down the exact extremal behavior of distance multiplicities, closing the gap between Erdos's n^{3+eps}, Guth-Katz's n^3 log n, and the possible n^3.
Sharpens the dual bound on distinct distances (t >> n/log n versus t >> n).
Bridges planar discrete geometry to classical analytic number theory via sums of two squares (r_2(m)).

proven: Guth-Katz upper bound sum f(u_i)^2 <= C n^3 log n (Annals of Math 181, 2015); axiomatized as guth_katz_theorem in erdos-95.
Erdos n^{3+eps} conjecture derived from Guth-Katz (erdos_conjecture_proved, erdos-95, 0 sorries).
Cauchy-Schwarz bridge (n(n-1))^2 <= t * sum f(u_i)^2 giving t >> n/log n (sq_sum_multiplicities_le, erdos-95).
Ramanujan asymptotic sum_{m<=x} r_2(m)^2 ~ c x log x, source of the lattice's log factor.
Convex-position case sum f(u_i)^2 = O(n^3) with no log (Altman 1963; convex_polygon_case, erdos-95).
open: Whether sum f(u_i)^2 <= C n^3 (no log) holds for all non-lattice configurations, and how to make 'non-lattice' precise (bounded additive energy / general algebraic position).
Whether the log n in the general upper bound is unavoidable at the level of the worst-case constant.
knownResults.goal: Formalize the lattice lower bound: define the sqrt(n) x sqrt(n) integer lattice as a PointConfig and prove sum f(u_i)^2 >= c n^3 log n, establishing that the log n cannot be dropped from the general Guth-Katz bound. Companion: state the precise non-lattice removability conjecture as a Lean proposition.
